label: Assumption audit
title: Assumptions and derived conclusions

checks.claim: The target is \(\Pi_N\propto e^{-V_N}\), with \(V_N(z)=\sum_iU(\theta,\sqrt N z^i)\).
checks.note: The entropy endpoint uses this actual lifted Gibbs measure. Its probability normalization is supplied by the lifted-target LSI premise.

checks.claim: The parameter noise is \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\), while physical particle noise is \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\).
checks.note: Exact coordinate update identities and the independent-Gaussian law identity connect the canonical Markov laws to the existing noise-driven implementation.

checks.claim: The lifted dimension is \(D=d_\theta+Nd_x\), and base smoothness \(L\) gives lifted smoothness \(NL\).
checks.note: The quadratic replicated-pair identity gives the gradient bound. Strong convexity is not needed for these identities or the LSI endpoint.

checks.claim: The actual lifted target satisfies \(2\beta H\le J\) with \(\beta>0\).
checks.note: IsLogSobolev includes probability normalization and tests strictly positive continuously differentiable relative probability densities. A pair-target LSI does not supply this premise here.
Compatibility is an explicit shared-argument input. The positive-step restriction is exactly the ULA restriction after substituting \(h=\gamma/N\) and \(\ell=NL\).

checks.claim: \(r_k(t)\Pi_N\) equals the actual frozen-drift Gaussian interpolation on \([0,\gamma/N]\).
checks.note: RegularInterpolationData supplies the density identification, strict positivity and spatial regularity. It does not construct the densities from smoothness and LSI.

checks.claim: Local domination and differentiability justify the derivative of \(\int r\log r\,d\Pi_N\).
checks.note: The local structure requires integrability, measurability, pointwise time derivatives and a common integrable derivative bound. Its neighborhoods are two-sided, including at zero.

checks.claim: The supplied weak identity is valid for the entropy test \(1+\log r\).
checks.note: The interface requires an identity for every continuously differentiable test with integrable displayed terms. The proof derives entropy production from this identity and Young’s inequality.

The shared Gaussian file proves joint displacement moments. Constructing the conditional drift field and transferring those bounds into the admissible weak equation remains an obligation of the supplied data.
A shared GibbsScore theorem proves the target gradient moment under its hypotheses. The endpoint does not assemble that result with an LSI-to-transport argument to derive this current-law comparison.
Finite KL is obtained from the regular density integral before using its real value. This prevents the infinity-to-zero behavior of ENNReal.toReal from making the bound vacuous.
The entropy derivative and recurrence are conclusions, not fields of RegularInterpolationData. The forcing identity cancels both particle factors from the squared step.
The geometric-sum envelope uses \(1-e^{-x}\ge3x/4\) for \(0\le x\le1/4\), giving the shared ULA constant \(8\).
Division by positive particle number normalizes both the initial contribution and the bias. This quantity is still full-state KL divided by particle number.

checks.claim: If \(\beta=N\alpha\), the normalized bias is \((8\gamma L^2/\alpha)(d_x+d_\theta/N)\) and the rate is \(e^{-\alpha\gamma k}\).
checks.note: The lifted LSI of strength \(N\alpha\) must actually be supplied. The step is then \(\gamma\le\alpha/(4L^2)\) and compatibility is \(\alpha\le L\). No shared-parameter tensorization is asserted.

checks.claim: Parameter KL is at most full joint KL; a bound \(H_k/N\le B\) gives parameter KL at most \(NB\).
checks.note: The reference is the parameter pushforward of the same lifted target. Finite joint KL gives finite marginal KL before real conversion.

checks.claim: The proved conclusion concerns sampling error in relative entropy.
checks.note: Neither LSI scaling alone nor normalized joint entropy supplies concentration around a marginal-likelihood maximizer. No optimization or MMLE error estimate is claimed in this extension.

verdict: This is a conditional IPLA entropy theorem derived in the repository through its proved ULA representation. All particle scaling identities, Gaussian-law identifications, entropy conclusions and marginal data-processing statements are proved. The actual lifted-target LSI and RegularInterpolationData remain explicit mathematical inputs; no pair-to-lift LSI transfer or optimizer concentration is claimed.
